mathdb.title: Termination conjecture for flips of klt pairs
mathdb.note: The page is the standard klt-pair termination conjecture with real boundary over a fixed base. Fujino, Introduction to the log minimal model program for log canonical pairs, Conjecture 3.15 and the following discussion (page 76), explains the reduction of ordinary lc termination to all-dimensional klt termination. Preserve the characteristic-zero, pair, coefficient and base hypotheses; this is not a claim about generalized pairs or other characteristics.

mathdb.title: Modularity of Elliptic Curves over Number Fields (End_K(E)=Z)
mathdb.note: The statement matches Thorne Conjecture 2.6. Thorne explains after Conjecture 2.5 that curves with complex multiplication defined over K have abelian Galois representations described by class field theory. The End_K(E)=Z restriction is therefore the standard remaining modularity scope, not an arbitrary narrowing. Preserve it exactly; geometrically CM curves may still satisfy End_K(E)=Z.

problems.title: Effective Mordell conjecture for curves of genus at least two
problems.scope: Construct an algorithm that, given a number field K, a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X/K of genus at least two and a finite number-field extension L/K, computes the complete finite set X(L). This algorithmic effective-Mordell form supplies an effectively computable height bound for each input curve and field; qualitative finiteness alone is insufficient. A prescribed linear or polynomial uniform height bound is a stronger formulation and requires an explicit scope decision.

mathdb.title: Algorithmic Mordell conjecture
mathdb.note: The full MathDB search located #332964, which states Algorithmic Mordell for all smooth projective geometrically connected curves of genus at least two over number fields, including finite extensions. It matches Conjecture 6.1 of Ariyan Javanpeykar, arXiv:1604.05043, and the basic algorithmic effective-Mordell form selected here. The discussion after that conjecture explains that computing all points supplies an effectively computable height bound but does not imply prescribed linear or polynomial dependence on the field discriminant or curve height. Stronger quantitative reference: [MathDB #318788 — Strong Mordell for families](https://mathdb.com/p/318788/strong-mordell-conjecture-for-families-of-curves); that family-uniform bound is not automatically included in this record. Former related page #393610 only asserts existence of a Vojta-type constant and is not this approved mapping. The 2016 source date is not asserted as the original conjecture date.
